messages.body_plain:
Hello, I am helping someone analyze their data which has been labeled with 3 types of isotope: light, medium, and heavy. We would like to run a linear mixed model with isotope as a random effect. Does MSstats support this type of analysis, or should we use lme4::lmer for now?

Thank you,
Brian Zhang

That you for your response. That correction worked and the function ran to completion. However, upon running the full pipeline I noticed 2 things:
My master mix channels were removed in the PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat output. Why would this be and how can I make it to keep my pooled channels? I did not see a parameter for this.
The batch correction was still present and the samples clustered at protein level by TMT kit and not by sample type. Do y'all have any recommendations for filtering missing values or specific settings for large data sets? I am trying not to impute missing values so that was set to FALSE as shown in the code below.
inputPD <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(
  PSMs,
  annotDB,
  which.proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions"
)

quant.pd.msstats <- proteinSummarization(
inputPD,
method = "LogSum",
global_norm = TRUE,
reference_norm = FALSE,
remove_norm_channel = FALSE,
remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
MBimpute = FALSE,
maxQuantileforCensored = NULL
)

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
messages.subject_clean: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
messages.body_plain:
PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat shouldn't remove any samples. Can you share the updated annotation file?

If your mastermix channel is used for normalization, then you should set the Condition and BioReplicate columns in the annotation file to "Norm" so that MSstatsTMT can recognize the mastermix channels. And then set reference_norm = TRUE in proteinSummarization to perform the normalization between runs based on the mastermix channels.
If you want to remove the PSM with any missing values in a run, you can set rmPSM_withMissing_withinRun = TRUE in PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat.

So as a summary, you can first  set the Condition and BioReplicate columns in the annotation file to "Norm", then run the following code

inputPD <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(
  PSMs,
  annotDB,

  which.proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions",
  rmPSM_withMissing_withinRun = TRUE
)

quant.pd.msstats <- proteinSummarization(
inputPD,
method = "LogSum",
global_norm = TRUE,

reference_norm = TRUE,

remove_norm_channel = FALSE,
remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
MBimpute = FALSE,
maxQuantileforCensored = NULL
)

messages.subject: Re: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
messages.subject_clean: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
messages.body_plain:
The annotation file shows channel 126 is the MasterMix sample. But in the example PSM file you shared, all the values in channel 126 is NA. I guess this happens throughout the whole data. PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat function of MSstatsTMT 1.6.3 removes the NA values from the output so you didn't see condition MasterMix.

MSstatsTMT currently relies on the reference channel (reference_norm method) to perform the normalization between runs, which removes most of the batch effects. I would recommend to use the mastermix for normalization and check whether the samples are clustered together to validate the normalization.

messages.subject: Repeated Measures design for MSstatsTMT
messages.subject_clean: Repeated Measures design for MSstatsTMT
messages.body_plain:
Hi MSstats group,

I have performed a multiplex TMT experiment in which I have made repeated measurements of some biological samples.

Our paper is currently under review and available online as a preprint:
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.08.06.239517v1

We performed a 16-plex experiment three times. In each experiment, we analyzed 2 mice -- a WT and Mutant mouse. In each experiment, we measured 7 subcellular fractions prepared from each of the two mice 1x. The remaining 2 channels in each experiment were reserved for analysis of  technical replicates of a pooled quality control sample for normalization. Previously I analyzed my data with the 'Sum + IRS + EdgeR' approach as you describe in your 2020 paper. Now, I would like to use MSstats as I acknowledge that it is the more appropriate tool.

But currently, I don't think MSstatsTMT this supports my experimental design.  I wrote a post on the `MSstatsTMT` github which gives a better description of my experimental design. I had not read your paper when I posted the issue however. So when I saw your 2020 paper online, I closed this issue, and read your paper. It answered may of my questions.

I wrote some code exposing the protein-wise modeling and statistical comparisons performed internally by MSstatsTMT so that I could try to understand what was going on and to try and pass a different model to accommodate my design. But, I still am struggling to perform the comparison I am interested in. Which is the comparison between the conditional means of WT and MUT mice adjusted for differences in bioFraction. Previously, I used a model of the form: (Abundance) ~ Fraction + Condition in EdgeR to assess this comparison.

Would you be willing to collaborate to try and make MSstatsTMT compatible with my repeated measures design?

Best,
Tyler

Hi Amandeep,

MSstats indeed identified these two technical replicates for biological sample UTR1. When MSstats shows the summary of samples, it calculates the mean technical replicates per condition (total number of MS runs/ total number of biological replicates). In your case, it is 4/3 =1.333 and becomes 1 after rounding  1.333. So this is just how MSstats summarises the annotation information.

messages.subject: Re: Interaction terms for a two factor and two level experimental design
messages.subject_clean: Interaction terms for a two factor and two level experimental design
messages.body_plain:
Dear Priya,

The (log)-fold changes alone are not particularly meaningful. E.g., a log-fold change of 2 may or may not indicate a systematic change between conditions (or a systematic interaction). This depends on the underlying variation. For proteins with large biological and/or technical variation this may be an artifact; for proteins with small variation this may be evidence of a systematic change. To make decisions, it is best to rank proteins by adjusted p-values.

HTH
Olga Vitek

> > The (log)-fold changes alone are not particularly meaningful. E.g., a log-fold change of 2 may or may not indicate a systematic change between conditions (or a systematic interaction). messages.subject: Issue with very high (~100) and negative LogIntensities
messages.subject_clean: Issue with very high (~100) and negative LogIntensities
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have been trying to use MSstats to process some MQ out files.

raw <- MaxQtoMSstatsFormat(
                           evidence=infile,
                           annotation=annot,
                           proteinGroups=proteinGroups,
                           removeMpeptides=TRUE,
                           removeOxidationMpeptides=TRUE
                           )

I have tested a few normalization strategies for DataProcess:

en_noNorm <- dataProcess(
                      raw,
                      logTrans = 2,
                      normalization = FALSE,
                      fillIncompleteRows = TRUE,
                      featureSubset = "all",
                      summaryMethod = "TMP",
                      censoredInt = "NA",
                      cutoffCensored = "minFeature",
                      remove50missing = FALSE,
                      address = 'io_files/MSstats',
                      maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999,
                      clusters = NULL
                    )

en_medNorm <- dataProcess(
                      raw,
                      logTrans = 2,
                      normalization = 'equalizeMedians',
                      fillIncompleteRows = TRUE,
                      featureSubset = "all",
                      summaryMethod = "TMP",
                      censoredInt = "NA",
                      cutoffCensored = "minFeature",
                      remove50missing = FALSE,
                      address = 'io_files/MSstats',
                      maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999,
                      clusters = NULL
                    )

en_gsNorm <- dataProcess(
                        raw,
                        logTrans = 2,
                        normalization = 'globalStandards',
                        nameStandards = 'sp|P00724|INV2_YEAST',
                        fillIncompleteRows = TRUE,
                        featureSubset = "all",
                        summaryMethod = "TMP",
                        censoredInt = "NA",
                        cutoffCensored = "minFeature",
                        remove50missing = FALSE,
                        address = 'io_files/MSstats',
                        maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999,
                        clusters = NULL
                      )

I extracted RunLevelData:

en_gs_tidy <- as_tibble(en_gsNorm$RunlevelData)

en_no_tidy <- as_tibble(en_noNorm$RunlevelData)

en_med_tidy <- as_tibble(en_medNorm$RunlevelData)

And I have found quite the spread in LogIntensities including values as high as 100 and as low as -237.
no normalization
min: -177
max: 100
Global standard norm
min: -227
max: 37.4
Median norm
min: -38.9
max: 32
Here is some session info, if that is helpful:

R version 3.6.3 (2020-02-29)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 10 x64 (build 18363)

MSstats_3.18.5

Any help would be welcome.

Thanks!
Matthew Waas
